title: Python SDK: ackable streaming chat envelope and coalesced-event ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: customers building long-running chat UIs and agent pipelines need an ergonomic Python surface that: (1) exposes per-event acknowledgements for durable sinks (DB / event bus), (2) supports coalescing of high-frequency token events into higher-level 'message' events to reduce churn, (3) has clear retry/idempotency semantics so downstream consumers can safely re-process, and (4) lets apps fallback to non-streaming completions when the stream fails mid-response.

Goal: design and implement an "ackable envelope" streaming API for the Python SDK that returns an async iterator of Event objects. Each Event contains a lightweight .ack()/.nack() API, an idempotency token, and a stable "coalesce_key" for grouping related low-level deltas into a single application-level message. Provide first-class helpers for: backpressure-aware consumers, automatic checkpointing, graceful streaming->batch fallback, and telemetry hooks for token/latency/cost breakdowns.

Why unique: existing stream surfaces tend to either (a) expose raw token deltas (too low-level) or (b) offer purely fire-and-forget callbacks. This ticket bridges the gap by giving app developers explicit control over commit semantics while keeping common patterns ergonomic (context managers, helper adapters).
acceptance_criteria: New API returns AsyncIterator[Event] where Event has attributes: type, delta, coalesce_key, idempotency_token, is_final, timestamp, and methods ack() and nack(reason)
SDK implements a Coalescer utility that groups sequential events with same coalesce_key into a single logical message object delivered after a debounce/window policy
Built-in consumer helpers: .checkpoint_every(n_events) context manager and .auto_ack(mode="on_commit" | "on_receive")

Failure modes: if network stream disconnects mid-response, SDK produces a 'partial_response' event with fallback instructions and emits a telemetry marker; customers can opt into an automatic non-streaming completion retry
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for ack/nack semantics, idempotency token replay, coalescing edge cases, and fallback behavior
Documentation page and one example app (chat UI) demonstrating ack flow and metrics integration
Design review approval recorded and PR merged with associated changelog entry for py-sdk-2.4.0
implementation_notes: Event object shape must be stable: uses simple dataclass with __slots__ to minimize allocations for high-throughput flows

ack()/nack() return awaitable; ack performs best-effort local checkpoint and enqueues durable commit to background worker (configurable sync/async), nack schedules exponential-backoff retry optionally with dead-letter hook
Idempotency token derived from (conversation_id, request_id, sequence_position) and also allowed to be provided by server if available
Coalescer is pluggable: default policy = time-window 35ms + max_tokens 64; allow user overrides via CoalescerConfig
Backpressure: provide optional bounded queue when converting streaming bytes->Event to avoid uncontrolled memory growth; SDK exposes .drain() hook for graceful shutdown
Fallback: if user opts into fallback=True, the SDK will issue a non-streaming /generate call with same prompt and return a synthetic final Event; record fallback_reason in telemetry
Telemetry: emit markers for stream_start, first_token, last_token, ack_latency_ms, fallback_taken; wire to existing telemetry client (trace_id propagation)
comments: 2026-01-28 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Draft design attached. Spikes planned to measure ack path cost (sync vs background commit).

2026-02-03 - Marco Gutierrez: Spike results: synchronous ack adds ~0.8ms median latency on hot path; background commit (batched) recommended for default. Added Coalescer spike; 35ms window reduced number of commit ops by ~6x for chat workloads.
2026-02-12 - Leah Kim (PM review): Requested explicit fallback opt-in and clear docs about semantic differences between auto_ack modes. Added acceptance criteria for fallback and telemetry markers.
2026-02-20 - Design review: Approved with minor suggestions: rename event.coalesce_key -> event.group_id for clarity; agreed to keep backward-compatible field alias for one release.

2026-02-28 - Engineering: First draft implementation pushed (PR #2764). Integration tests added for ack/nack and idempotency token replay. Edge case: server-supplied idempotency tokens occasionally absent; SDK must synthesize deterministic token.
2026-03-05 - QA: Found flakiness when coalescer window configured to 0ms under high concurrency; mitigation: enforce minimum 5ms debounce and stronger ordering guarantees in coalescer queue.
2026-03-09 - Release lead (Olivia Chen): Requested changelog blurb and example notebook. Preparing docs and migration notes for users of lower-level token streams.
2026-03-10 - Marco Gutierrez: PR merged (2764). Follow-up tests in PR 2771. Next: walkthrough with client engineering and include sample chat UI in examples/ackable-chat.
example_code:
from redwood import StreamingClient

async def consumer():
    client = StreamingClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
    async for event in client.chat.stream(conversation_id="conv-123", fallback=True):
        # coalesced message appears when coalescer flushes or is_final==True
        if event.type == "message":
            print("MESSAGE", event.coalesce_key, event.delta)
            # durable sink: ack only after DB write succeeds
            try:
                await write_to_db(event)
                await event.ack()  # returns when local checkpoint scheduled; durable commit runs in background
            except Exception as e:
                await event.nack(str(e))  # triggers retry flow (exponential backoff)
        elif event.type == "partial_response":
            # stream interrupted, app can choose to wait for fallback or trigger UI fallback
            schedule_fallback_prompt(event)
notes_for_review: Please validate API names: Event.group_id vs coalesce_key (design suggested group_id). We will keep both properties (alias) for one release to ease migration.
Consider exposing a 'commit_mode' option at client-init: 'background_batch' (default), 'blocking_sync', 'best_effort'
We must add a small migration guide for existing users of low-level token iterators; include code recipe to wrap old streams with Coalescer to get same app-level events
